claim: Sliding-window attention (w=64 + 1 sink, computing 44.3% of full causal's attention entries at T=256) beats full attention on final val loss at tiny scale on natural text
design: grid (attention x 10 seeds), PAIRED analysis: each seed fixes both data order and init, so lanes differ only in the attention op
scope: gpt2 2-block d=128, T=256, TinyStories, 400 steps, AdamW@1e-3 (the S3-lrxopt safe quadrant), batch 4. Mechanism NOT established (regularization story is interpretation); budget-conditionality unknown — exact may catch up at longer budgets; window size unexplored beyond w=64. Throughput not significantly different (reference implementation materializes [T,T]; the fast kernel belongs to coalfire). MECHANISM AMENDED 2026-08-06 by S1b-window-monotone: the 'locality is a favorable inductive prior' reading is WITHDRAWN. Loss falls monotonically as the window shrinks (w=16 < 32 < 64 < 128 < exact, every adjacent contrast signal), so there is no interior optimum and no evidence for a locality-matched prior at this scale. The empirical effect stands; the explanation does not. Budget-conditionality is under test in experiments/sparse_s1_budget. SUPERSEDED 2026-08-07: the 400-step measurement below is correct and stands, but the comparison REVERSES by 1200 steps (exact ahead, Delta +0.0123) so the headline reading 'sliding window beats full attention' is budget-conditional and must not be cited as a general ordering. See S1c-budget-reversal.
note: Referee review (2026-08-05) downgraded the n=3 version to pending: paired t=-3.39 at df=2 was below the 4.303 two-tailed critical value and the direction had NOT been pre-specified (the manifest expected match-or-cost), so no one-tailed reading was licensed. Seed extension to n=10 pairs settles it two-tailed: t=-10.35 (df=9, crit 2.262), swa better in 10/10 seeds, mean gap -0.0479 nats. The n=3 heterogeneity (-0.0208 outlier) was seed noise, not fragility. Sparsity is real in this cell: w=64 at T=256 computes 44.3% of full causal's attention entries. Two analyses, both significant, reported to avoid confusion: PAIRED (registered t=-10.35, df=9) exploits the shared seed/init design; UNPAIRED pooled (t=-4.19, df=18) is what tools/atlas_analyze.py and reproduce --check-only compute, since the generic analyzer cannot assume pairing. The conservative number clears its bar too. 2026-08-06: mechanism claim removed per the S1-b pre-registered decision rule, which committed us in advance to amending this row if P3 held. It held. 2026-08-07: superseded per the S1-c pre-registered decision rule for P2, committed before those runs.

claim: Loss falls MONOTONICALLY as the attention window shrinks, down to 12.3% density: w=16 (3.785) < w=32 (3.822) < w=64 (3.852) < w=128 (3.894) < w=256=exact (3.899). No interior optimum exists above w=16, which falsifies the locality-as-inductive-prior explanation of S1-swa-beats-exact
design: grid (window x 5 seeds), PAIRED against the S1 w=64 and exact anchors at matched seeds; headline effect is w=16 minus w=64
scope: gpt2 2-block d=128, T=256, TinyStories, 400 steps, AdamW@1e-3, batch 4, sinks=1. LIMITATION STATED IN THE PREREG: a monotone curve down to w=16 is also consistent with an interior optimum BELOW 16 (w=8, w=4, w=1) — this cell cannot separate 'capacity artifact' from 'optimum lower than we looked'. The discriminating test is budget, not another window rung.
note: Registered under a pre-registration committed to git BEFORE the runs (b2f44e4) with the direction fixed in advance; P2 (H-PRIOR, interior optimum) and P3 (H-BUDGET, monotone) were declared mutually exclusive at the w=16 rung, and the decision rule bound us to amend S1-swa-beats-exact if P3 won. It won and the row was amended. Also carries the in-situ harness verification: swa@w=256,sinks=1 reproduced the exact lane BITWISE (diff 0.00e+00, all 5 seeds) through 400 steps of real training, so the equivalence pin holds outside the unit test.

claim: The sliding-window advantage over full attention is a SHORT-BUDGET artifact that reverses with training: paired Delta (swa@64 - exact) moves from -0.0472 at 400 steps to +0.0123 at 1200 steps, a change of +0.0595 in the same direction on every seed. At this scale the SIGN of a sparse-vs-dense comparison depends on where you stop
design: two budgets (400 from experiments/sparse_s1, 1200 fresh) x 2 attention lanes x 5 shared seeds; the registered effect is the paired per-seed CHANGE in Delta, which is the quantity the hypothesis is about
scope: gpt2 2-block d=128, T=256, TinyStories, AdamW@1e-3, batch 4, swa w=64 sinks=1. Both lanes were still improving at 1200 (no early stop, 12 evals, loss ~3.86 -> ~3.59), so this is the still-training regime, not an overfitting artifact. STATISTICAL PRECISION: the SHRINKAGE is established two-tailed (t=5.09, crit 2.776); the REVERSAL itself (Delta(1200)>0, t=2.74) clears the one-tailed crit 2.132 but NOT the two-tailed 2.776 — the one-tailed reading is licensed only because P2 committed the direction to git before the runs. Does NOT establish that any published result is wrong; the general claim is about reporting discipline (state and vary the budget), not other people's conclusions.
note: Registered under a pre-registration committed before the runs (8a01a92) that named this cell as the discriminating follow-up inside the S1-b document BEFORE S1-b's result was known — so it is not a post-hoc rescue of a story that had just broken. The pre-registered threat (both lanes stalling early, making this an overfitting comparison) was checked and did not materialise. Supersedes S1-swa-beats-exact. Programme consequence: 'beat sliding-window' is now an under-specified target for V2/CoD, which must be compared at >=2 budgets with both reported, fixed in its pre-registration before it runs.

claim: The attention sink is INERT at this scale: removing it moves val loss by +0.0003 at 400 steps (t=0.16) and -0.0001 at 1200 (t=-0.03), against a capacity-model prediction of ~0.0008 made and committed BEFORE the runs. Both prior S1 findings (window monotone, budget reversal) reproduce without the sink — they are properties of the window alone. The reversal without sinks clears the two-tailed bar outright (+0.0122, t=2.89), which the sinked version did not
design: swa(w=64, sinks=0) at steps {400,1200} x 5 seeds, paired against committed sinks=1 and exact anchors at matched seeds; the registered effect is the sink's own contribution (sinks0 - sinks1 at 400), whose predicted value was ~0.0008 — a null was the PREDICTION, with a pre-committed 0.008-0.021 grey zone that would have read as inconclusive
scope: gpt2 2-block d=128, T=256, TinyStories, AdamW@1e-3, batch 4, w=64, one sink vs none. Does NOT license 'sinks don't matter' in general — sinks earn their keep in streaming/long-context regimes this cell does not touch. Magnitude caveat: 0.0003 and the predicted 0.0008 are indistinguishable at this resolution; what is confirmed is a null where a null was predicted. EXECUTION NOTE: first run lost to WSL /tmp cleanup after completion; rerun to persistent storage reproduced the surviving numbers exactly (deterministic seeds) — recorded in the manifest.
note: First QUANTITATIVE prediction in the programme to survive contact with data: the capacity model (H-BUDGET, established by S1c-budget-reversal) predicted the sink's effect from its density contribution alone (0.58pp -> ~0.0008 nats) and was right at both budgets. This promotes it from explanation-left-standing to model-with-predictive-content. Also certifies the cross-engine vehicle: sinks=0 is the only configuration coalfire.cpp can express, and every S1 finding reproduces in it.

claim: B*(256) -- the budget where exact attention overtakes swa(w=64,sinks=1) at d=256 -- is a DISTRIBUTION over seeds, not a point: at 3600 steps the pooled n=15 sign is undetermined (Delta +0.0195, SD 0.0377, t=2.00 < two-tailed 2.145, split 9+/6-), per-seed persistent-crossing budgets span 1600-3600 with 6/15 seeds never crossing, and both prongs of the pre-committed dispersion criterion (|mean|<SD, minority>=4/15) are met. The budget-conditionality direction itself (shrink = Delta(3600)-Delta(1200) > 0) replicated on 10 virgin seeds for the FOURTH pre-committed time: mean +0.0541, t=4.13, clearing even the unlicensed two-tailed bar
design: 10 NEW paired seeds {6..15} x 2 lanes (exact, swa) at the sparse_s1_boundary protocol, pooled with the 5 boundary seeds after a 10/10 pooling-licence gate; primary H-CROSS-15 two-tailed on n=15, H-SHRINK-4 one-tailed (direction committed pre-data, licence caabe19) on the 10 new seeds alone as an independent fourth replication; V-DISPERSION criterion fixed pre-data
scope: gpt2-nano d=256 L=2 heads=8, T=256, TinyStories slice + chat7b vocab (cap 4096), AdamW@1e-3, batch 4, swa w=64 sinks=1, CPU numerics, house protocol. STILL-TRAINING REGIME THROUGHOUT: best_val landed within the last 3 evals in 14/15 seeds, so overfit onset was never reached and the dispersion is not an overfitting artifact. Fifteen seeds bound dispersion at ONE width; nothing here says whether dispersion grows with d (transfer_s1's F3 question). No claim about published sparse-attention results at scale; the general-methods claim remains budget-AND-seed reporting discipline.
note: Completes the S1 arc (S1 -> S1b -> S1c -> boundary -> here) and formalises the seed-lottery exhibit at n=15 under pre-registration: mean Delta marches monotonically upward across all nine 400-step slices while SD roughly doubles, so early unanimity (15/15 at b=400) is the cheap wrong signal and dispersion is what budget buys. Any single-number crossover-budget claim is now a MEASURED under-specification, not a methodological preference. Feeds transfer_s1's power section (SD(3600)=0.0377, SD(1200)=0.0214, b0 spread 1600->never) and forces its F3 layer to treat B* as a per-seed distribution at both scales.

claim: Across a 2x width change (d=256 -> 512) the SIGN of every pairwise lane comparison in a six-lane attention panel is preserved at matched validation-loss position, while the scalar effect sizes are uncorrelated: F1 sign-pattern concordance 1.000 over 15 cells (seed-bootstrap band [0.867, 1.000]; threshold 0.75, band low > 0.50) and H-SCALAR Spearman rho = -0.082 over 15 edges. Framing: width preserves the TOPOLOGY of the comparison graph (edge orientations) and destroys its METRIC (magnitudes, trajectory shapes, crossover budgets). NARROW BY MEASUREMENT: the 15 cells are fifteen edges at ONE milestone (the S slice-800 level), because at the protocol's fixed lr=1e-3 the M arm reaches only the first of five S milestones (see T1-fixed-lr-mistunes). Robustness variant at fixed steps 0.681 (not adopted); F2 modal shape-class agreement 9/15; F3 crossover moves later with width (S crossed 11/12, M 4/12).
metric: F1 sign-pattern concordance at matched val-loss milestones (seed-majority edge orientations)
design: Pre-registered 31 Aug 2026 (experiments/transfer_s1/PREREGISTRATION.md, analysis script committed with it; amendment 1 and clarifications 1-8 dated): arms S (d=256) and M (d=512), six lanes (exact; swa w=16/32/64/128 s=1; swa w=64 s=0), 12 seeds each, 3600 steps, lr 1e-3 fixed across widths; positions matched by S-arm L1 median val-loss milestones; F1 adopted iff >= 0.75 with bootstrap 2.5th pct > 0.50; H-SCALAR foil |rho| < 0.5; bridge gate passed; drift guard 12/12; regime check per lane; L4 GPU throughout with bit-identical checkpoint-resume across Colab prunes
scope: gpt2-nano family, layers=2, T=256, batch 4, lr 1e-3 FIXED across widths (a declared protocol property, not a muP answer), TinyStories slice + chat7b vocab (cap 4096), CUDA (L4) venue, d in {256, 512}. Threat 2 (regime) FAILS at M in every lane: best val plateaus at a median 0.89 of the run (never earlier than 0.67), so every statement is scoped to the matched-milestone positions, which lie inside the still-training regime. L (d=1024, 3 seeds, one edge) reaches no milestone at lr 1e-3 (overfits from ~step 2700) and is a trend point only: fixed-step M vs L 1.000 over 9 cells, S vs L 0.444.
note: Outcome one of the three named in the pre-registration ('structure transfers while scalars do not'), licensed at its measured width: one shared position. The fixed-step robustness failure is the matched-position rule's own prediction (equal steps are different places on different curves). The claim's narrowness is a property of the protocol, not the phenomenon; transfer_s2 (lr set per width by a fixed rule) is the study that can test it at five positions.
reproduce: python3 experiments/transfer_s1/analyze.py --arms S=<S root> M=<M root> L=<L root>  (each root holds runs/<run>/events.jsonl; the analysis prints the milestone band reached per arm)

claim: A learning rate held fixed across widths (1e-3, the transfer_s1 protocol property) mis-tunes the larger widths: the d=512 exact lane bottoms out at a median best val of 3.72 against 3.35 at d=256 and reaches only the first of five S-arm milestones (12/12 seeds at slice-800, 0/12 at the rest); d=1024 reaches none and overfits from about step 2700. At lr=5e-4 the d=512 lane reaches all five milestones (final val 3.18-3.23, below S). The sign pattern on the exact-vs-swa64s1 edge is itself lr-sensitive at fixed width: 16/27 fixed-slice sign agreement between lr 1e-3 and 5e-4 (seeds 21-23: 6/9, 8/9, 2/9).
metric: milestone band reached (seeds whose exact lane reaches each S milestone); best val; fixed-slice sign agreement across lr
design: The pre-registered Threat 4 sensitivity cell (sweep_M_lr.json: d=512, lr 5e-4, L1 and L4, seeds 21-23) run after arm M was banked, compared with the same seeds of arm M at lr 1e-3; the milestone band printed by analyze.py (execution clarification 8) for S, M and L
scope: Same protocol as T1-structure-transfers. Descriptive by pre-registration: the cell cannot change any primary reading. It changes the weight of the scope line: 'lr fixed across widths' is the reason the matched band collapses to one position, and it is the muP objection materialising as measured.
note: Motivates transfer_s2 (PREREG_DRAFT.md): per-width lr selected by a rule fixed in advance. Stage 1 of that study (12 Sep 2026) selects lr*(256)=2.5e-4 and lr*(512)=5e-4 by the rule; the base width was not at its best rate either (1e-3 gives 3.369 vs 3.228 at 2.5e-4).

claim: At d=256, exact attention's lead over swa(w=64, sinks=1) keeps widening after both lanes pass their held-out minima: no second crossing through 12000 steps (H-SECOND-CROSS not supported; one significant sign change, between b=1000 and b=4000), the overfit-order condition fails (exact reaches its minimum first in 2/10 seeds against a registered 8/10), and the undetermined zone closes at b=4000. Crossing-theorem assumption (iii) is not falsified at this protocol through 12000 steps.
metric: val loss difference L_swa - L_exact at b=12000
design: grid (attention: exact, swa) x 10 new seeds {41..50}, 12000 steps, eval every 200; pre-registered with analyze.py (licence 89760cd); Amendment 1 (pre-data) set checkpoint_every 400, nothing else
scope: gpt2-nano d=256 L=2 heads=8, T=256, batch 4, AdamW@1e-3, swa w=64 sinks=1, TinyStories slice + chat7b vocab (cap 4096), CUDA venue on L4. Overfit regime reached in 10/10 seeds. Bounded to 12000 steps at this scale; says nothing about non-nested comparisons, where the theorem does not apply.
note: Falsification test of atlas/THEOREM_CROSSING.md assumption (iii); joint-outcome row 'not supported / not supported': the monotone regime extends. The S1e zone, still open at 3600 with n=15, closes here at 4000 with ten new seeds; the W-CHECK prediction (~2610 steps) is consistent with the observed zone width (1000 to 3000 steps on the 1000-step grid).

claim: With the learning rate set per width by a rule fixed in advance (2.5e-4 at d=256, 5e-4 at d=512), the sign structure of the six-lane attention panel does not meet the registered transfer criterion: concordance 0.700 over the four milestones meeting the registered reachability condition (42/60; the frozen script's five-milestone output is 47/75 = 0.627) against the 0.75 threshold, and the later-milestone falsifier fires (0.733, 0.667, 0.467). This is the outcome of the registered decision rule, not a statistical exclusion of transfer: the post-hoc seed-bootstrap band of the four-milestone reading is [0.583, 0.833]. Post hoc, concordance falls from 0.933 at the first milestone to 0.467 at the fourth, eleven of the eighteen disagreements are reversals, and the lane a d=256 screen would pick (w16+s) has the lowest seed-mean loss at d=512 through the third milestone and the highest of six at the fourth (regret 0.059).
metric: F1 sign-pattern concordance at matched val-loss milestones (seed-majority edge orientations)
design: Pre-registered 12 Sep 2026 with a falsifier (experiments/transfer_s2/PREREGISTRATION.md, analysis script frozen at the licence commit; Amendment 1 dated): stage 1 selects lr per width on the exact lane by a mechanical rule; stage 2 re-runs the transfer_s1 panel (six lanes, 12 seeds, 3600 steps) at the selected rates; milestones, foil, guards and thresholds as transfer_s1
scope: gpt2-nano family, layers=2, T=256, batch 4, rate per width by the registered rule, TinyStories slice + chat7b vocab (cap 4096), CUDA (L4) venue, d in {256, 512}; the d=256 arm reaches the fifth milestone in 8/12 seeds (below the registered 9), so the primary reading is the four admitted milestones. The studies vary the rate and the reachable band together, so they do not show whether a shared rate would also lose agreement at later positions.
note: Supersedes T1-structure-transfers' 'structure transfers' reading: T1 measured real agreement at the one milestone the larger width could reach under a shared rate, where T2 also finds near-complete agreement (0.933); with both widths through the band, agreement does not hold. Reported in 'The Confounder Both Arms Shared' (submitted to Machine Learning, 9 Oct 2026).

claim: At depth 2, learned highway gating shows no resolvable difference from the hardwired residual skip (Delta1 = +0.0044 at 400 steps, 95% CI [-0.0095, +0.0183], t = 0.88; -0.0101 at 1200 steps, CI [-0.0305, +0.0104], t = -1.37, two-tailed df=4 critical 2.776), while any skip connection is worth 1.2-1.5 nats over a plain stack (plain minus residual +1.208 at 400, +1.497 at 1200, the gap growing with budget).
design: Pre-registered archaeology pilot (experiments/registry_0001_highway/PREREGISTRATION.md, analyze.py committed pre-data): three lanes (highway, residual, plain) x 5 paired seeds, 1200 steps; Q1 estimation framing, Q2 descriptive
scope: TinyStories, d=128, 2 blocks, 1200 steps, 5 paired seeds; the 66K gate parameters neither help nor harm here. Depth 2 is the null-region check the dossier predicted; the depth-4/6 rungs, where the 2015 mechanism claims to earn its keep, are open. Flex family with learned positions in every run, so unaffected by the RoPE head-coverage defect.
note: First entry of the architecture-archaeology registry (registry/0001_highway_networks/ENTRY.md section 7). A null at this protocol and scale, not a verdict on the 2015 regime.

claim: Crossing width (256, 512) with learning rate (2.5e-4, 5e-4) at four fixed loss targets gives the pre-registered reading MIXED: H-POS is supported at 5e-4 (S5 vs M5: 0.933 at t1, 0.733 at t4) and not at 2.5e-4 (S25 vs M25: 0.967 over t1-t4, band [0.850, 0.983]); H-RATE is supported at width 256 (S25 vs S5: 0.900, band [0.767, 0.950]) and not at 512 (M25 vs M5: 0.717). Descriptively, the three pairs that decline are exactly those that include the width-512 panel at 5e-4; at a shared 2.5e-4 the ordering carries from 256 to 512 through all four targets.
metric: F1 sign-pattern concordance at fixed exact-lane loss targets (seed-majority edge orientations)
design: Pre-registered (experiments/transfer_s3/PREREGISTRATION.md, licence f61e253, analysis committed with it, smoke-tested on every branch): six width x rate cells of the six-lane panel x 12 seeds, two new (S5, M25: 144 runs) and four reused from Studies 1 and 2; binary bridge bit-identical; one execution clarification (four runs re-run after a relay overwrote their logs; results identical)
scope: gpt2-nano, layers=2, T=256, batch 4, TinyStories slice + chat7b vocab (cap 4096), CUDA (L4); widths 256 and 512, rates 2.5e-4 and 5e-4 (1e-3 descriptive), targets 3.7539, 3.5152, 3.3491, 3.2392. The 'includes M5' pattern is post-hoc and descriptive.
note: Bears on T2-structure-position-fragile and on the account in 'The Confounder Both Arms Shared' (at Machine Learning): the late disagreement of Study 2 belongs to the width-512 panel at the rate Study 2's rule selected; it is not a general decay along the loss curve.

claim: Rejection-sampling SFT filtered by a synthetic judge does not teach the model to fool that judge more than SFT on samples filtered with the judge's confusion rates placed at random: judge-truth gap J - R = +0.004 (95% CI [-0.007, +0.016], t 0.84) at q=0.10 and +0.005 ([-0.017, +0.027], t 0.51) at q=0.25. Falsifier F-PT2 fires at both rates: at this step and scale, judge error behaves like label noise.
metric: judge_truth_gap (frozen judge reward minus exact-match truth on the test set)
design: Pre-registered six-arm comparison (E, J10, R10, J25, R25, X; equal arm size per seed), licence e10514e, frozen analysis, run from a clean clone
scope: tinyarith R=20, llama-tiny d=128 L=2 (~1M params), base 3000 steps, one round of rejection-sampling SFT (600 steps), 8 samples per training fact; synthetic judges with declared rules (cue and near-miss acceptance at q, no false rejections); 10 paired seeds. Nothing about LLM judges, larger models, iterated rounds or preference optimisation.
note: A registered null: the pre-registered falsifier of the provenance thesis at the rejection-sampling step. PT5 tests the same thesis on preference optimisation.

claim: Exact-match-filtered rejection-sampling SFT beats synthetic-judge-filtered SFT on held-out truth accuracy: E - J10 = +0.059 (95% CI [+0.017, +0.101], t 3.17) and E - J25 = +0.097 ([+0.061, +0.132], t 6.10, 9/10 seeds). Exact filtering lifts accuracy from 0.371 (base) to 0.445; judge filtering at q=0.25 ends below the base (0.348), as does its noise-matched twin (0.353).
metric: truth_acc (exact match on the frozen test set)
design: Secondary hypothesis H2 of the pre-registered PT2 design (licence e10514e)
scope: tinyarith R=20, llama-tiny d=128 L=2 (~1M params), base 3000 steps, one round of rejection-sampling SFT (600 steps), 8 samples per training fact; synthetic judges with declared rules (cue and near-miss acceptance at q, no false rejections); 10 paired seeds. Nothing about LLM judges, larger models, iterated rounds or preference optimisation.

claim: Under its pre-registered rule the reward-hacking monitor was NOT validated (MONITOR_BLIND): GRPO on a +1-shifted reward key raised the monitored rate M (answers a+b+1) by +0.126 (t 2.27, df 4, crit 2.776) with 0/5 seeds above the base+3SD threshold (0.486), and closing the channel lowered it by +0.101 (t 1.98). Diagnosis: the base model already answers a+b+1 in 13-35% of samples (about 40% of its errors), so the channel coincided with its commonest error and no base-relative threshold could separate hacked from base; three seeds learned the hack (M +0.18 to +0.24, truth about 0.38 to 0.23), two did not move.
metric: M = fraction of dev samples the shifted key accepts and exact match rejects
design: Pre-registered open/closed GRPO falsifier of the monitor, 5 paired seeds, licence d70bbcd, frozen analysis, clean clone
scope: tinyarith R=20, llama-tiny d=128 L=2, base 3000 steps; GRPO group 8, 4 prompts/step, beta 0.05, lr 1e-3, 300 steps open then 300 closed; one constructed channel (+1 shift). Nothing general about reward-hacking monitors.
note: A registered negative of the test design, not of the monitor statistic, which tracked the training reward exactly. PT4b re-runs it under a fresh pre-registration with a shift the base rarely produces.

claim: The reward-hacking monitor (fraction of samples the training reward accepts and exact match rejects) detects a reward channel that pays for a specific wrong answer and registers its closure: GRPO on a +2-shifted reward key raised the monitored rate M from 0.034 to 0.237 (paired +0.203, t 5.20, df 4; 5/5 seeds above the base+3SD threshold 0.121) while truth fell from 0.435 to 0.130, and correcting the key lowered M by 0.131 (t 3.82).
metric: M = fraction of dev samples answering a+b+2 (shifted key accepts, true key rejects)
design: Pre-registered open/closed GRPO falsifier of the monitor, fresh seeds 211-215, shift chosen before licence from PT4's base models only (licence 00327d4), PT4's frozen analysis unchanged
scope: tinyarith R=20, llama-tiny d=128 L=2, base 3000 steps; GRPO group 8, 4 prompts/step, beta 0.05, lr 1e-3, 300 steps open then 300 closed; one constructed channel (+2 shift, base rate 0.4-7.8%). Validates the monitor against rewards that pay for specific wrong answers where truth is checkable; nothing about hacks without a truth signal.
note: Answers PT4-hack-monitor's negative: the monitor statistic works; PT4's +1 channel was the base's commonest error, so its test could not fire.

claim: Under the research vocabulary (first 4096 tokens of chat7b.gguf), 19.09% of the 400,001 tokens every Atlas, sparse-attention, transfer and highway run trained on map to <unk> (21.30% in the held-out tail); the bare full stop, comma, double quote, '!' and '?' are absent from the vocabulary, and 1503 of its 4095 non-<unk> entries carry attached punctuation that the trainer's tokenizer never produces.
metric: unk_rate (tokens mapped to id 0) on the trainer's token stream
design: Descriptive measurement, replicated three ways: the trainer's C++ tokenizer header, a byte-exact Python mirror on corpus bytes rebuilt from the pinned public revision (sha256 equal to the retained historical file), and the earlier transfer_s2 post-hoc measurement
scope: tinystories_slice_v1 (corpus/registry.jsonl) read to data.max_tokens=400000; vocab_chat7b_cap4096_v1. Common to every lane and width of the studies that used it, so it bounds what their absolute losses mean and does not by itself reverse a paired lane comparison.
note: Replicates the 9 Oct 2026 measurement reported in the transfer paper (19.1% overall, 21.3% held out).
